rows.quote: The publicly available R10 data from the FinnGen study comprised 4620 patients with VTE and 356,574 healthy controls.[21] In contrast, the VTE-related GWAS data from the UK Biobank, obtained from Neale labs, consisted of 4620 cases and 356,574 controls, encompassing 11,901,177 SNPs, and utilizing the disease code ukb-d-I9_VTE (https://gwas.mrcieu.ac.uk/).
rows.coder_note: Step 2 of the decision order (release identifier, rule A): 'R10 data from the FinnGen study' names release R10. The 4620 cases and 356,574 controls given for FinnGen are endpoint counts, are not stated as a release N and identify no other FinnGen row (rule H), so step 1 does not apply; reference 21 (Kurki 2023) is shared by all FinnGen rows and does not conflict. Accession, rule C4: ukb-d-I9_VTE in the same passage sentence is the UK Biobank dataset's, not this row's.

Step 1 of the decision order (rules I3, C4, H). Accession, rule C4 second case: ukb-d-I9_VTE has the prefix ukb-d, which the row 'MRC-IEU UK Biobank GWAS pipeline (OpenGWAS ukb-b)' lists, but the sentence (p003, sentence 3) attributes the data to Neale labs and gives 4620 cases and 356,574 controls, in all 361,194, which that row does not allow (463,005 or 337,092) and which is exactly the N of 'Neale lab UK Biobank GWAS round 2'. The accession and the counts point to different dictionary rows.
